subject: Magna Corp — Operational failback windows & multi-region capacity commitments
messages:
From: Lila Sharma <lila@magna-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: magna-corp-pmo@magna-corp.com
Date: 2028-04-01T16:12:00Z
Subject: Clarification on failback windows and RTO/RPO commitments for Magna RFP

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks again for the detailed RFP submission yesterday. The procurement team had a couple of follow-ups specifically around operational failback and the sequencing assumptions in section 4.3 of your submission. Two items we need clarified before we proceed to the sourcing committee: 

1) You reference a 4-hour RTO for critical transaction paths when a cross-region switchover is triggered. Can you confirm that this 4-hour RTO includes time for failback to the primary region (i.e., full restore + verification), or is it recovery-to-operations in the secondary region only?

2) There is a statement that failback windows will be scheduled during business off-hours and require a staggered capacity reservation for both regions. Please provide the minimum reserved capacity (vGPU-equivalents) you require in primary vs secondary to guarantee the stated RTO/RPO.

Also attach any runbook excerpts that show the verification gates we would use to sign off on failback completion. We need this for our technical approval.

Best,
Lila Sharma
Program Manager, Cloud Resilience
Magna Corporation

[Procurement thread id: MAG-RFP-042]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lila Sharma <lila@magna-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, magna-corp-pmo@magna-corp.com
Date: 2028-04-01T18:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on failback windows and RTO/RPO commitments for Magna RFP

Lila —

Appreciate the quick read-through and good questions. High-level answers up-front, attachments below, then a short breakdown: 

- The 4-hour RTO quoted is recovery-to-operations in the secondary region (i.e., service available on the failover region). Failback to primary is a separate operation and has its own window — we aim to complete controlled failback within 12 hours from the initiation of the failback procedure for the full-flanked path (verification included).

- Minimum reserved capacity: for steady-state heartbeats + canary traffic we'll need 40% of peak production vGPU capacity in the secondary when maintaining hot-standby (recommended for <1h automated switchover). For scheduled failback operations we recommend reserving an additional 30% burst capacity in the primary for a 6-hour window to speed sync/restore; total suggested reservation during failback = 70% of peak in primary (30% burst + 40% baseline).

Attached: multi-region-failover-matrix.pdf (capacity mapping), magna-operational-commitments-20280401.xlsx (table of commitments, trigger conditions), runbook-extract.txt (verification gates and manual steps).

Breakdown (short):
- Failover (primary -> secondary): automated switchover tested to target RTO=4h for core APIs, RPO=15 min for transactional store when KV-prefix caching enabled. This assumes hot-standby with live replication and KV syncs working at 2x normal replication throughput.
- Failback (secondary -> primary): sequence is: freeze writes on secondary, final replication flush, integrity verification, canary traffic cutover back to primary, progressive traffic ramp, post-cutover verification. Because we allow full data consistency checks and progressive ramping, we publish a separate target window of 12 hours to allow verification and rollback options.

If you want shorter failback (e.g., target 6 hours), we can support that with tighter pre-provisioned burst agreements and an expanded automation runbook; that impacts cost and needs a committed reserved capacity uplift.

Connor O'Brien
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Clarification on failback windows and RTO/RPO commitments for Magna RFP

Lila / team —

Adding operational context from an SRE perspective to Connor's excellent summary: 

1) The cited RPO=15min is achievable for transactional workloads when customers enable async MVCC replication with our prioritized log shipping. Without that, RPO degrades toward 1–2 hours. We'll include a short checklist in the runbook extract showing the replication mode toggle and monitoring queues to watch.

2) For the failback reserved capacity numbers, the 70% primary reservation during the failback window reflects the need to perform parallel data validation and run canaries without impacting production throughput. Example: if you have 100 peak vGPU units, we'd ask for 40 units warm in the secondary, plus a 30-unit burst allocation in primary for the 6–12 hour failback window.

3) Operational exception policy: If telemetry shows replication lag > 45 minutes during failback prep, we will halt automatic failback and require a staged manual approval from the customer's runbook approvers (we note this in the attached runbook-extract.txt under "Verification gates").

I've also flagged two optional mitigations that reduce failback time by ~40%: pre-snapshot accelerated sync (costed) and cross-region delta-transfer compression (turned on by default for accounts with >2TB daily change volume). Details in the workbook.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Lila —

One more technical note from infra/compilation side that may impact the procurement sizing decision: 

- RTO/RPO assumptions are influenced by model KV cache behavior during switchover. For models with >8k context and active long-lived KV states, cold-start token overhead increases. Practically, that means the 4-hour recovery target assumes either (a) per-model warm caches replicated across regions, or (b) rapid on-demand caching with pre-warmed checkpoints. If you cannot commit to warm-cache replication for all models, please identify the top-10 latency-sensitive routes you expect to prioritize; we can show a per-route capacity and cost differential.

- For failback sequencing, our recommended automation flow includes: 
  * Step 1: Quiesce write traffic to a stop window (we provide a traffic drain script).
  * Step 2: Final KV snapshot + checksum (sha256) and transfer to primary.
  * Step 3: Integrity verification (checksum match threshold >99.999%), then canary to 1% traffic for 30 mins.
  * Step 4: Progressive ramp (1% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) with health checks at each stage.

If Magna wants a formal appendix that ties the model classes to specific capacity numbers and expected token-warmup times, I can produce a short technical addendum. That addendum would show expected token generation lag per model size (7B, 13B, 70B) and recommended pre-warm reservation.

—Aditya
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
